headline: Approved 10 city staffing changes, including two part-time police officers and a new Deputy HR Director.
summary: Alderman Vincent said the city should let its recent compensation study work before making more position changes. Human Resources Director Jamie Corwin said the changes respond to job duties, not individual employees, and he endorsed all of them.
decisions: Approved a grade 120 Business Services Manager in place of a grade 117 Office Manager in Planning and Community Development. No vote count was recorded.

Approved Welfare Department changes: raising a Welfare Specialist I from grade 108 to 110, eliminating a part-time Accounting Technician II, and adding a part-time Accountant I. The changes add $3,500 to the salary line. No vote count was recorded.
Approved creating two part-time Police Officer positions, grade 117, for a new staffing initiative pilot program.
Approved adding a grade 124 Finance Manager - Treasury and eliminating a grade 108 Accountant I. No vote count was recorded.
Approved adding a grade 104 Administrative Assistant I and eliminating a grade 104 Accounting Technician I in the EPD division. No vote count was recorded.
Approved adding a grade 110 Irrigation Designer and raising the Vegetation Specialist position from grade 106 to 107. No vote count was recorded.

Approved adding a grade 118 Community Health Nurse II, two grade 108 Environmental Health Technicians, and an amendment to the Community Health Nurse I class specification. No vote count was recorded.
Approved adding a grade 121 Water Distribution Engineer and eliminating a grade 118 Water Distribution Manager. No vote count was recorded.
Approved changing the Independent City Auditor position to grade 130. No vote count was recorded.
Approved adding a new full-time Deputy HR Director, grade 127. No vote count was recorded.

## COMMITTEE ON HUMAN RESOURCES/INSURANCE

November 17, 2026 at 6:00 PM

Chairman Goonan called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen Goonan, Sapienza, O’Neil, Burkush, Vincent

Messrs.: J. Belanger, C. Michaud, M. MacLeod, J. Corwin

1. SmartShopper Report for the third quarter of 2026.

(Note: Provided for informational purposes only; no action is required.)

- 2. Communication from Jeff Belanger, Planning and Community Development
- Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Add one (1) full-time Business Services Manager, grade 120;

• Eliminate one (1) full-time Office Manager, grade 117.

Matthew Normand, City Clerk: Additionally, this is contained in this letter, the department is requesting the creation of an alternate title line on the class specifications for Planner III and Planner IV positions, to be retitled Senior Planner and Chief Planner, respectively.

Alderman Sapienza: Jeff, could you just explain in your own words what's going on here? I mean, I know it's on the agenda. I'm assuming there's obviously a cost item to this.

Jeff Belanger, Planning and Community Development Director: For one of them, for the business services manager instead of the office manager, yes. There's no cost item for the planner positions. Those are simply name changes.

Alderman Sapienza: So with respect to that, that first one that's going from grade 117 to 120, what is the impetus for that?

J. Belanger: The duties of that position have substantially increased beyond what is specified for the office manager. So it's now much more in line with the business services manager.

Alderman Sapienza:. Duties have increased with dilapidated housing and whatnot?

J. Belanger: The position does a lot of things, but the main increase has been in the financial responsibility. So financial analysis, accounts payable, accounts receivable, planning for the budget. There's a range of different financial responsibilities that are not contained within the office manager position.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman O’Neil , it was voted to approve.

3. Communication from Charleen Michaud, Welfare Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Modify one (1) current full-time Welfare Specialist I position from a grade 108 to a grade 110;

• Eliminate one (1) part-time Accounting Technician II position, grade 107; • Add one (1) part-time Accountant I position, grade 108.

Alderman Sapienza: I have the same question I had for Mr. Belanger. Can you just explain why we're going from grade 108 to grade 110?

Charleen Michaud, Welfare Director: Sure. I'm actually going to introduce Mark MacLeod. He will explain those differences.

Mark MacLeod, Welfare Supervisor: For the welfare specialists I, over the last several years we've added duties to that role. We’ve expanded coordination with Families in Transition to enter our homeless families and clients into the HMIS system, which is a homeless tracking system, which puts them on track to get into public housing or section eight. We switched over some duties that used to be part of the welfare specialist III, where she handles the yearly record retention and purging project. So that was typically handled in the past by a much higher grade, the welfare specialist III. She has created and maintained our digital signage, which gives resources and upcoming events to the clients. And some of the other biggest changes that she has added is we used to do non- direct handoffs with homeless clients to shelters. We've created a direct line of communications where she does the direct referrals from the front; something like that typically could have been done by a welfare specialist II. She's taken those added duties on. Additionally with that she set up kind of a workflow with another outside agency outside of the town which helps people get housing and find housing resources all over the city.

C. Michaud: So to make it a little more simplified, this position is the person at our front desk. For many years, this job was done by a person who was a welfare specialist III. When that person left the position, we downgraded it to a welfare specialist I, realizing that the person who is brand new to this job was not going to be able to do all of the things that a person with 30 years of experience used to do. But over the last several years, as her experience has increased, we've added back in a number of those duties. We're not looking to raise this back up to a two or a three, but we are looking to raise up the pay grade. There's also our software system, which is new to the office, which has also added additional data entry responsibilities. And it's going to cost all of 60 something dollars a week. Both of these position changes combined are only going to add $3,500 to our salary line item and we have the ability to meet that.

Alderman Vincent: This isn't necessarily directed at Welfare; it's more of a generalization of what we've got on our agenda here tonight. I understand we just did a compensation study. I think what needs to be known is that we just paid a lot of money as a city to have a compensation study done. Tonight is a very wide array. But there seems to be constant changes to personnel, whether it's a new grade, a new position. In my opinion, it's an ugly look because we just spent all that money on a compensation study. We should at least let that ride its wave for a while to see how that works into play before we start manipulating all these positions. I've been sitting in this chair for a couple of years now, and it's just a constant grade change, position change. I'm really starting to wonder what our real reasons for doing this are. Do we not know these positions well enough at the time, or the people in those positions? Or are we just moving people around because they're doing a good job or giving them more money? I don't know what the reason is, but I just want it to be known that in my opinion, it's not a good look to have constant changes within our departments on position and pay numbers when we just paid a ton of money to have a compensation study done. Now, I'm not saying these aren't necessary. Please don't take it that way, but to the public that doesn't know the inner-workings of these departments, we're setting ourselves up as aldermen to answer these questions on your behalf. Well, it's a needed thing. Well, it's a grade ten now. They don't know what that means. Half the time we don't know what that means until you explain it to us. If you tell me, this job pays $26 an hour, now he's making $32 an hour, now I can put some substance behind that. I don't hold with me a chart on what each grade scale is, but I'm telling you, I can't help but state that we're not giving the compensation study its due to work out, and then we make the maneuvers as we can. But if we're constantly shifting and moving left and right, what the hell was the purpose of the study for if we're not adhering to our own voice of what we wanted, which was to bring us to that next level. It's not towards anybody. When I saw this agenda, the first thing that came to my mind was what are we doing here? And it's constant. I mean, we are constantly manipulating our organizations to meet these requirements. So if somebody is doing better now than they were two years ago, two years from now, they're going to be better than they were now. So are we going to move them again? Today we say no, but next year, next month, whenever, we realized they're doing more, we need to do this. I would like to see more stabilization within our own organizations. I don't know too many other people and businesses out there that can manipulate as much as city departments can, but I'm hoping that this is the last big push in this realm for this, at least for a while. And again, I'm sorry if I'm stepping on your toes, Alderman Sapienza, but you're going to ask the same question of every department, and I think that's just what it is. This is a lot, my friends. It's a lot. I just want to make sure that we're really looking at the big picture here and not just moment at times every couple of weeks. We didn't see that last week. Let's change it. We didn't see that the week before. Let's change it. Look at your departments. That's what the compensation study was. Look at your departments. Know your people, know their jobs, know their strengths and weaknesses, and put them in the right jobs. And then we don't have to keep doing this because it's just too erratic. I apologize for the harshness. It's just the way I see it, my friends, that's all.

Chairman Goonan: Jamie, would you like to say anything about that? I assume all these positions and these changes, and I'm not sure if it's because we have that new compensation study and, it's absolutely not perfect, but we are trying to finally set where these jobs should be, not just by the compensation study, but by the desk audits and the rest of the stuff that goes on. Talking to some of the department heads that bring these jobs up and talking to the HR Director, there's a basis for these changes. They're not changes just because someone needs a raise or someone needs to be a little bit more than someone else. But it seems like there's a lot of thought put into this.

Jamie Corwin, Human Resources Director: The compensation study is a bit dated. And all compensation data when it comes to you is outdated the minute it's printed. And so, as a new HR director coming into the city, I've been going out and meeting with each of the departments and learning about all the different things that they do within their special bubble. And it's become clear that in many cases, there were some things with the comp study that weren't necessarily really understood in full the way that they should have been. There's also been change even within the last year or two with the scope of work. So compensation is kind of an art and kind of a science. So it's never going to be perfect. There will always be slightly adjusting changes. These are not meant to address people- specific issues. They're meant to adjust scope of work duty-related issues to keep people in the appropriate place based on the scope of duties in their role.

Alderman Vincent: I get all that. I don't think it's good to say the compensation study is inadequate. We just had it done. So we still need to give it its workings. And just to be clear, I wasn't saying that I don't accept these. I'm going to approve all of these. But at the end of the day, we shouldn't be inundated and you should not be inundated as the HR Director with all these constant changes. Look at your people. Look at your positions. Figure it out. Now, we shouldn't have this again for a while. I get one or two, but if you're a department and it's consistent, then I'm questioning what we're doing. I just can't help but question that. I get the scope of duties change, because everything changes. But if you're doing a job, the scope of duties are what they were hired for. If those duties change, then the position will change, but not every so many months, and it's not at a consistent level where the departments need to constantly reinvent these positions. And again, you're throwing out numbers, Grade 120 and Grade 117, 107, 110, moving from 108. Give us more meat than this. Maybe that'll make it easier if you say the guy is working 45 hours a week and we're paying them way too little. Okay, well, let's revise the whole thing and let's look at it again. And the next person you put in that shouldn't be in that same situation. Does that make sense? I'm trying to make your job easy, too, because you're kind of like the conduit. You're the one that's feeding this and honestly, you’ re HR, but do you really know what goes on inside these departments? You're working at it and it's great. But if a director comes to you and says, my goodness, this guy's working a ton of hours, we really need to take care of it. What do you need? And then you're a conduit until you really understand the internal workings, and you're not expected to know what goes on to that level, you're not there. That's why they have directors.

J. Corwin: I conduct desk audits. I am going in and I'm looking at their duties. I'm doing market analysis. I'm looking at lots of different things. So it's not just someone says, hey, let's take a look at this, this is what I want it to be. It's using a variety of resources.

Alderman Vincent: This current compensation study that we're on right now that just got approved, what was the effective date of that?

J. Corwin: July 1, 2025.

Alderman Vincent: We're still in the infancy stages of this. I just want us to give it a chance and then we can rework this. But it's consistent, this committee is consistently making changes to positions. And again, it's not anyone in particular. I'm just saying it's a consistency. That to me tells me we're not doing something right. We're missing something that we can do better. And everybody says the same thing. Well, it's not going to cost anything, so what are we doing? Are we robbing Peter to pay Paul? Because if you're giving somebody more money, who aren't we paying? Or are we saying, well, we got a vacancy, so we're just going to use that money to give it to them. Now we're playing numbers that we don't need to be doing. That's my perception, and somebody that's watching at home right now, that's what they're looking at.

Alderman O'Neil: I know the effective date was July 1st, but the work into the study goes back years before that. A lot of it had to be negotiated. It's about retention or attracting people because employees are looking for the money. That's the fact of life right now. And we either invest in people, we encourage it, and it's a good thing that we have movement through the city. I think of how many people are scattered now that came out of Finance at one time that are in departments all over the city in the finance role, and some of them are moving on to other departments now for a higher grade, that's a good thing that our employees want to advance in their careers. I think the reality, and not to put Charlene on the spot, how much of this is about retention?

C. Michaud: For these two positions, these are our two highest turnover positions since 2019. In the welfare specialist I position we've had five different employees; in the account tech position, we've had six different employees.

Alderman O'Neil: We've got to remain competitive. I think the consultant did a good job but not a perfect job. And the market continues to not be favorable to us. And that's the reality of this. I support the department heads. It's not an easy decision for them to come in to ask for these changes. I think they're well thought out and reviewed with HR. So I understand Alderman Vincent's frustration, but we've got to remain competitive. We're going to lose people or we're not going to be able to attract people. Talk to Public Works about attracting truck drivers and laborers. We're not competitive. We think we are, but we're not to the private sector. And they don't worry about health insurance. They don't worry about paid vacation. They don't worry about paid holidays. That used to be a big attraction to become a city employee. Not anymore. It's about the money.

Alderman Sapienza: Do you give a blanket endorsement to all of these on the agenda? Are there any that you are against?

J. Corwin: I have kicked some back and rejected things before they would even reach this agenda. Certain things are just not at the point where I agree that there's enough change to warrant making the change.

Alderman Sapienza: Do you endorse all of these that are on tonight's agenda? That's what I meant. You don't have any reservations about any of these recommendations on tonight's agenda?

J. Corwin: No. I've spent the last several weeks working on all of these.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

4. Communication from Ken Loui, Assistant Chief of Police, requesting the creation and addition of two (2) part-time Police Officer positions, grade 117, to the department's complement as part of a new staffing initiative pilot program.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman O’Neil , it was voted to expedite the committee’s report to the full Board.

5. Communication from Sharon Wickens, Finance Officer, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Add one (1) full-time Finance Manager - Treasury position, grade 124;

• Eliminate one (1) full-time Accountant I position, grade 108.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to approve.

6. Communication from Robert Robinson, EPD Chief Engineer, requesting the following changes to the division's complement:

• Add one (1) full-time Administrative Assistant I position, grade 104;

• Eliminate one (1) full-time Accounting Technician I position, grade 104.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman O’Neil , it was voted to approve.

7. Communication from Mark Gomez, Chief of Parks, Recreation & Cemetery, requesting the following changes to the division's complement:

• Addition of one (1) new full-time Irrigation Designer position, grade 110; • Amend the Vegetation Specialist position from a grade 106 to a grade 107.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to approve.

8. Communication from Anna Thomas, Public Health Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Add one (1) new full-time Community Health Nurse II position, grade 118; • Add two (2) new full-time Environmental Health Technician positions, grade 108; • Amend the Community Health Nurse I position class spec content

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman O’Neil , it was voted to approve.

9. Communication from Phil Croasdale, Water Works Director, requesting the following changes to the department's complement:

• Add one (1) new full-time Water Distribution Engineer position, grade 121; • Eliminate one (1) full-time Water Distribution Manager position, grade 118.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman O’Neil , it was voted to approve.

10. Communication from Emily Rice, Solicitor, requesting the Independent City Auditor position be modified to a grade 130.

On motion of Alderman O’Neil , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

11. Communication from Jamie Corwin, Human Resources Director, requesting the addition of one (1) new full-time Deputy HR Director position, grade 127, to the department's complement.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to expedite the committee’s report to the full Board.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Sapienza , duly seconded by

Alderman Vincent , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee
